problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{ln⁡(x)},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=e.$

feedback.problem:
If a curve $C$ is given by $y=\frac{{2}^{x}}{{x}^{2}-1},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=0.$

The slope at $x=0$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $y$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={2}^{x}$ and $v(x)={x}^{2}-1.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{({2}^{x})}^{′}\cdot ({x}^{2}-1)-{2}^{x}\cdot {({x}^{2}-1)}^{′}}{{({x}^{2}-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{x}ln⁡2\cdot ({x}^{2}-1)-{2}^{x}\cdot 2x}{{({x}^{2}-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{x}[({x}^{2}-1)ln⁡2-2x]}{{({x}^{2}-1)}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=0$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\,(0) & =\frac{{2}^{0}[({0}^{2}-1)ln⁡2-2(0)]}{{({0}^{2}-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-ln⁡2}{1} \\  & =-ln⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line at $x=0$ is $-ln⁡2.$
